newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, November 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, November 5.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Members of opposition voice increasing dissatisfaction with Public Works minister and former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro and may ask for him to resign (all).

* Financial police say former head of state railway was "protected" in a corruption probe involving bribes scandal centred on Enimont, the chemical business unit created by agro-industrial company Montedison and state energy giant Eni (all).
* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema says Italy should seek a two-turn electoral system. Prime Minister Romano Prodi had proposed to abolish proportional representation (all).
* For the first time in the history of the Italian Republic, a woman, Fernanda Contri, will sit among judges in the Constitutional Court (all).
* Shopkeepers across the country protested against planned increases in taxes threatening "tax obstruction" (all).
* Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco says the "Euro-tax" will be a one-off, will not hit consumer spending or workers' 13th-month special payment and will be less heavy than people are estimating (all).
* Cerus, holding company owned by Carlo De Benedetti agreed to sell its stake in Valeo car parts maker to CGIP and others (all).
* European Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Italy should privatise state telecoms group Stet and motorway management and construction company Autostrade by 1997 spring (all).
* Foreign trade minister Augusto Fantozzi says Italy's export can sustain a mark/lira central parity at 1,000-1,050 lire (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
